messages:
anya: fyi new onboarding sample "edge-worker" is failing strict builds for TS users targeting Cloudflare/worker runtimes. looks like typing + esm/cjs resolution friction.
anya: error: `TS2769: No overload matches this call` on our client.fetch wrapper when passed a platform Request-like object.
maya: do you have the repro? which tsconfig are they using?
anya: user uses next + edge runtime, tsconfig: module=ESNext, moduleResolution=Node, lib: ["ES2020"], types: [] — they don't include DOM lib (assume fetch/request from runtime).
sam: missing DOM lib is a common footgun. but even when they add DOM, we still see mismatch between NodeFetch types and platform Request (shape differs).
devon: overloads are the culprit. our typings export overloads: (input: string) | (opts: { input: string }) | (req: Request) | <T>(payload: T). Multiple overloads cause TS to pick a strict one when moduleResolution differs.
akira: maybe make a single discriminated generic: `fetchClient<T extends string|Request|RequestLike>(payload: T): Promise<ResponseLike>` and export a RequestLike interface that is structural. avoids relying on global Request ctor.
anya: good idea. but also should we ship our types with `typesVersions` to redirect older TS?
maya: typesVersions helps for TS older compilers, but not mixing runtime defs. I think docs + example tsconfig is lower friction: recommend moduleResolution: "Bundler" or NodeNext for edge builds, and include "DOM" lib.
devon: runtime detection: do NOT use `instanceof Request` (breaks across realms). use duck-typing: `isRequest = (x:any) => typeof x === 'object' && 'url' in x && 'headers' in x`.
sam: also watch out for `isolatedModules: true` in some builds — it disallows const enums and TS-only constructs in declarations; ensure our d.ts are emit-friendly.
akira: we should run a matrix of type-check CI: node-cjs, node-esm, edge-bundler, and a fast worker/deno target. catch these early.
anya: creating a small example in /examples/edge-worker-typing that demonstrates 3 tsconfig variants and a README with minimal changes to fix types. will link PR.
maya: another note: tsserver in editor sometimes picks node typings from @types/node which define a fetch polyfill now; cause ambiguous Request types. consider adding `types: []` in our published package to avoid leaking node types?
devon: we can't control user tsconfig, but we can add JSDoc in our README about conflicting @types/node. also include a `types` entry in our package.json that points to a compatibility d.ts with structural types.
anya: what about `unknown` vs `any` surface? currently our helper `parseInput` casts to any then passes through. should tighten to `unknown` and narrow with predicates so downstream inference stays useful.
sam: yes — prefer `unknown` on public API generics and only use `any` in internal low-level adapters. note that widening to any makes overload resolution worse for consumers.
akira: lint rule idea: ban `any` in d.ts files and forbid `instanceof Request` in source. add to codeowners for SDK.
sdk-bot: ticket RW-8820 opened for edge-typing-repro. CI job 4892 added: types-matrix (node-esm, node-cjs, edge-bundler).
anya: i'll draft the PR with: single structural generic signature, RequestLike interface, duck-typed guards, example tsconfigs, and CI job. will include changelog entry.
devon: let's aim for a patch/minor release depending on changes. if only internal guards + d.ts tweaks, minor. if we replace overloads with a new signature that affects inference, might be minor.
maya: can you also add a snippet for editors: `// in tsconfig.json: { "compilerOptions": { "moduleResolution":"Bundler", "lib":["ES2020","DOM"], "types": ["node"] } }` and explain why bundler helps.
anya: thanks team — opening PR in ~1h. :rocket:
